title: Moussaka
subtitle: Greek baked aubergine and lamb mince with béchamel
excerpt: Layers of fried aubergine, spiced lamb mince in tomato sauce, and a thick, golden béchamel, baked until set and bubbling. The centrepiece of Greek home cooking.

recipe.sourceNotes: Moussaka is the most internationally recognised dish of Greek cuisine, though related layered dishes using aubergine, minced meat, and béchamel are found across the Balkans and the Middle East under various names. The Greek version was refined and standardised by the Greek chef Nikolaos Tselementes in the early twentieth century, who added the béchamel topping that distinguishes the Greek version from simpler Balkan versions. The dish draws on both the Ottoman culinary tradition (spiced minced meat, aubergine) and French influence (béchamel from French culinary training). A good moussaka is a three-day project: the components are made on successive days and assembled. In practice, making all elements on the same day, assembling, and baking produces an excellent result.

recipeTools.notes: A deep baking dish, about 30 x 20 cm.
For the mince sauce and the béchamel.

content.text: Salt the aubergine slices and leave for 20 minutes, then pat dry before roasting. The moisture drawn out of the aubergine by the salt prevents it from absorbing excessive oil during cooking. The mince sauce must be cooked until very dry and well-seasoned: too much liquid in the mince layer makes the moussaka watery after baking. The béchamel should be thick enough to sit on top of the mince without running through; beat in eggs to help it set when baked.

items.preparation: or Kefalotyri if available; grated, for the topping

content.text: Salt the aubergine slices and leave for 20 minutes. Pat dry. Brush with olive oil and roast at 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6 for 20 minutes until golden. Set aside.

Brown the lamb mince in a saucepan over high heat. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes. Add the tomato puree, cinnamon, allspice, and cook for 1 minute. Add the wine, tinned tomatoes, and bay leaves. Season with salt. Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the sauce is thick and dry.

Make the béchamel: melt the butter in a saucepan. Add the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the milk. Simmer for 5 minutes until thick. Remove from the heat, stir in the nutmeg, and beat in the eggs.

Layer half the aubergine in a large baking dish. Spread over all the mince. Layer the remaining aubergine on top. Pour over the béchamel and smooth flat. Scatter with grated cheese. Bake at 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4 for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and set. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.
